I feel like I'm close. The app is no longer crashing when it tries to access the DB. In the heroku logs, it claims to be connecting to something!

"2025-02-19T06:59:36.851528+00:00 app[web.1]: 2025/02/19 06:59:36 [QGTUNNEL] Got new connection from {IP HERE}"

Any assistance would be greatly appreciated. Thank you for your time. 

Kind regards, 

Tristan Robertson

subject: Help with SOCKS5, SFTP and Ruby
description:
Hi Michael,

In order to work with a payment provider (Airplus) we need to connect to a SFTP server through static IP addresses. Therefore I recently subscribed to QuotaGuard Shield through a Heroku addon (app "kactus").

We use Ruby, but I have some difficulties to make it work with your proxy.

Here is a minimalist working example with a throw-away SFTP server that doesn't filter IPs, and WITHOUT proxy :

```
require "net/ssh"
require "net/sftp"

Net::SSH.start("ssh-pierre-hurtevent.alwaysdata.net", "pierre-hurtevent", port: 22, password: "%PZpH3QgezYe^a9Xd@4&") do |ssh|
  puts "inside SSH block"

  ssh.sftp.connect do |sftp|
    puts "inside SFTP block"

    sftp.dir.foreach("/") do |entry|
      puts entry.longname # ==> OK ! HERE I SEE THE FOLDERS LIST
    end
  end
end

```

But if I want to go through the QuotaGuard proxy, nothing happen (I use the Net::SSH::Proxy::SOCKS5 class and port 1081):

```
require "net/ssh"
require "net/ssh/proxy/socks5"
require "net/sftp"
require "uri"

quotaguard = URI("socks://14p22jkjmq81hg:ypbx6gxh9k7t6nf6qx1cfqguey8l@eu-west-shield-02.quotaguard.com:1081")

proxy = Net::SSH::Proxy::SOCKS5.new(quotaguard.host, quotaguard.port, user: quotaguard.user, password: quotaguard.password)

Net::SSH.start("ssh-pierre-hurtevent.alwaysdata.net", "pierre-hurtevent", {
    port: 22,
    password: "%PZpH3QgezYe^a9Xd@4&",
    proxy: proxy
}) do |ssh|

  puts "inside SSH block"

  ssh.sftp.connect do |sftp|
    puts "inside SFTP block"

    sftp.dir.foreach("/") do |entry|
      puts entry.longname
    end
  end
end
```

I'd like to note that I don't want to develop with gqtunnel for now:
 - If I understood correctly, I don't really need it because the Ruby libs I use support sending requests via a proxy (like net/ssh and net/sftp do)
 - I'm developing on a Mac M1, on MacOS, and the gqtunnel executable does not support it.

Thanks for your help!

--
Pierre Hurtevent

Hi Michael,

In order to work with a payment provider (Airplus) we need to connect to a
SFTP server through static IP addresses. Therefore I recently subscribed to
QuotaGuard Shield through a Heroku addon (app "kactus").

We use Ruby, but I have some difficulties to make it work with your proxy.

Here is a minimalist working example with a throw-away SFTP server that
doesn't filter IPs, and WITHOUT proxy :

```
require "net/ssh"
require "net/sftp"

Net::SSH.start("ssh-pierre-hurtevent.alwaysdata.net", "pierre-hurtevent",
port: 22, password: "%PZpH3QgezYe^a9Xd@4&") do |ssh|
  puts "inside SSH block"

  ssh.sftp.connect do |sftp|
    puts "inside SFTP block"

    sftp.dir.foreach("/") do |entry|
      puts entry.longname # ==> OK ! HERE I SEE THE FOLDERS LIST
    end
  end
end

```

But if I want to go through the QuotaGuard proxy, nothing happen (I use the
Net::SSH::Proxy::SOCKS5 class and port 1081):

```
require "net/ssh"
require "net/ssh/proxy/socks5"
require "net/sftp"
require "uri"

quotaguard = URI("socks://
14p22jkjmq81hg:ypbx6gxh9k7t6nf6qx1cfqguey8l@eu-west-shield-02.quotaguard.com:1081
")

proxy = Net::SSH::Proxy::SOCKS5.new(quotaguard.host, quotaguard.port, user:
quotaguard.user, password: quotaguard.password)

Net::SSH.start("ssh-pierre-hurtevent.alwaysdata.net", "pierre-hurtevent", {
    port: 22,
    password: "%PZpH3QgezYe^a9Xd@4&",
    proxy: proxy
}) do |ssh|

  puts "inside SSH block"

  ssh.sftp.connect do |sftp|
    puts "inside SFTP block"

    sftp.dir.foreach("/") do |entry|
      puts entry.longname

  end
end
```

I'd like to note that I don't want to develop with gqtunnel for now:
 - If I understood correctly, I don't really need it because the Ruby libs
I use support sending requests via a proxy (like net/ssh and net/sftp do)

My requirements:

Could you please confirm if any of your plans (QuotaGuard Static or QuotaGuard Shield) would fit these needs? If so, could you provide details on pricing and any potential limitations?
Thank you in advance for your assistance. I look forward to your response.

  Best regards,
João Maia
